title: Offers
summary: Diceroll's five offers as one parity table: each row is an offer defined once (what it sells, one-time or subscription, a quantity) and each set-up storefront is a column holding that offer's SKU as a chip, including the paid app itself on Steam and itch.io. Import and suggest surfaces an unmapped Google Play product, and the 3.1.3(b) warning asks for an App Store SKU.
compare: One row per offer, each defined once: name (the row's link to the editor), then what it sells (Tier Standard, Add-on Dice skins) and its billing (one-time, monthly with a 7-day free trial) or quantity (25 per purchase).

One column per storefront that is set up (App Store, Google Play, Steam, itch.io), in the canonical order with the store mark in the header; Microsoft Store, not set up, has no column and is named once in the table foot with Set it up.

A SKU is a mono chip: a green tick when the product exists on the store, an hourglass in info while it is in review, a dashed ring where Polaris Key can't check purchases (itch.io). App Store chips show only the part after the shared bundle prefix ('.full', '.plus.monthly'); the prefix 'com.example.diceroll.*' is named once under the App Store header, and the full id is the chip's tooltip and what Copy copies.
The paid app itself is a SKU: Steam's 'app · base game' and itch.io's 'app' sell the Full game offer, beside the App Store and Google Play in-app purchases that sell the same Standard tier.
Where a store can't sell an offer's kind, the cell says why in plain words (No subscriptions, No consumables, Game only), never a blank or n/a.
A missing SKU the rules need is a warning chip 'Create' on the App Store column for Neon dice pack, matching the 3.1.3(b) warning callout above the table with Create on App Store.

Import and suggest: a store product sold with no offer is a danger callout naming the SKU and what happened to the buyers, with one action, Add to an offer, which maps the SKU and re-verifies those purchases in the same change ('Add it to an offer and those 3 players get it at once'; commerce.add-to-offer). No separate mapping page or re-verify step exists.
State is status text: On sale (green) or Draft (muted with a pencil). No prices appear in the table.
Page actions are Import from stores (results: commerce.offers-import) and New offer (primary, commerce green; commerce.offer-new). With no offers the page is the empty state (commerce.offers-empty).

Phone: each offer is a stacked row, never a sideways table: name and state on the first line, what it sells under it, then one line of store marks, each with its SKU's glyph (tick, hourglass, warning 'Create', dashed ring, or a muted 'n/a' where the store can't sell that kind). Tapping a row opens the editor; the callouts' actions go under their text and the foot keeps only the legend.

Brand v2 shell (lead B2–B5, 2026-10-09): the work sits on the inset canvas with a 3px rule in the page's context accent (full-bleed below 1024); one orientation line (context chip + crumbs, never 'Platform' on a product page, no eyebrow repeating the path); h1 36/44 on a collection, 32/40 on a record, 24/32 on a phone; the one filled primary is ink; focus, hover, checked and selected take the accent of the service the element references (B17), never a status colour; the selected nav item is the subtle fill with a 3px marker; card heads are bands with no numerals; route tabs are an underline tablist with a 3px indicator; tables with filters are one workbench band; weights 400/500/600.
Search and the facet chips sit on one bordered band with the table (admin-3-13); the one attention card and New offer as the one primary stay.

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Fixed: phone rows are stacked with store marks, App Store chips show the part that differs, the holiday_bundle fix is one action, and New offer, Import, Add to an offer, Create on App Store and the empty page are drawn.

findings.issue: [phone] The parity table shows the Offer column and part of App Store only; Google Play, Steam, itch.io and State are off-screen and the chips are cut twice.
findings.resolution: Below 640px each offer is a stacked row: name and state, what it sells, then one line of store marks each with its glyph (tick, hourglass, warning Create, dashed ring, muted n/a). No sideways scroll. Compare item 10 updated.

findings.issue: [visual / scannability] Truncating from the start cuts each App Store id at a different character, so the column looks broken and the differing part stays buried.
findings.resolution: Chips show only the tail after the bundle id ('.full', '.skins', '.plus.monthly', '.rerolls25'); 'com.example.diceroll.*' is named once under the App Store header with a tooltip; the full id is each chip's tooltip and what Copy copies.

findings.issue: [flow] The danger callout asks for two manual steps (add the SKU, then re-verify), and no offer exists for holiday_bundle.
findings.resolution: The callout now reads 'Add it to an offer and those 3 players get it at once.' Add to an offer opens one picker, drawn as commerce.add-to-offer: a new offer from holiday_bundle (default) or an existing offer as a second Google Play SKU; one change maps the SKU, re-verifies the 3 purchases and updates those licenses, and the toast says '3 players now have Holiday bundle'.

findings.issue: [flow / missing states] New offer, Import from stores, Create on App Store and the empty Offers page are not drawn.
findings.resolution: Added commerce.offer-new (What it sells, an empty 'Set a base price', Create on App Store / Google Play rows, a Steam copy card with a DLC picker, itch.io explained), commerce.offers-import (suggestions with Dismiss and Add offer, one unmatched product pointing at Licensing, Add all 3), commerce.create-iap (L1 caution confirm: product id, type, price point, territories, Apple's never-reused rule) and commerce.offers-empty.

findings.issue: App Store header's second line breaks the header baseline and collides with Google Play at 1024.
findings.resolution: Subtitle removed (tooltip only); every store header is one line; columns are at least 130px wide at the smallest table width.

findings.issue: Tablet header collisions and clipped chips.
findings.resolution: Below 1040px the matrix is card rows (label 90px, value flex, two columns from 640px); no column dropped.

findings.issue: Needs attention rows are long, repeat the table and word holiday_bundle two ways.
findings.resolution: '3 players bought holiday_bundle and got nothing' with Add to an offer; 'Neon dice pack needs an in-app purchase (App Review 3.1.3(b))' with Create on App Store; count chip removed for two rows; 'since Oct 5' dropped.

findings.issue: Three phrases for not applicable, duplicated offer name, mismatched legend and Microsoft line.
findings.resolution: One muted dash with the reason in a title; sub-lines 'Add-on · one-time'; legend and Microsoft Store line share a colour and show at every size.

findings.issue: Two equal stacked buttons on phone.
findings.resolution: New offer is the one full-width primary; Import from stores is a text link under it.

findings.issue: [wide 1920] Console pages stretch tables and attention rows across the whole width.
findings.resolution: Page content is capped at 1280px, left-aligned, from 1600px (.cm2 page cap); attention text is capped at 72ch with its action beside it.

findings.issue: Row sub-lines and legends are small, and chevrons and copy icons have small hit areas.
findings.resolution: Sub-lines and legends are at least 12px (13px here) in the muted token that already passes 4.5:1; icon buttons have a 24px target; one table header token and row height are shared.

findings.issue: Drop the Billing filter chip, or the State and Billing chips.
findings.resolution: declined: Billing is a real offer attribute shown in the Offer sub-line and useful to filter by. The chips are a kit pattern, not a spacing problem.

findings.issue: Merge Billing and itch.io into one 'Other stores' cell at tablet.
findings.resolution: declined: Merging stores into one cell hides data and breaks the matrix; the card-row reflow keeps all of them.
